vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: plausible-analytics
Version: 1.0.1

The OpenClaw skill bundle for Plausible Analytics is benign. All scripts (`breakdown.mjs`, `realtime.mjs`, `stats.mjs`) correctly interact with the Plausible Analytics API (`https://plausible.io/api/v1/`) using the provided `PLAUSIBLE_API_KEY`. Input arguments are safely incorporated into URL parameters using `URLSearchParams` or `encodeURIComponent`, preventing URL injection vulnerabilities. There is no evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, arbitrary code execution, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts against the OpenClaw agent in the `SKILL.md` file. The code strictly adheres to its stated purpose of querying Plausible Analytics data.

llm.summary: This skill uses your Plausible API key to query website analytics and shows no hidden persistence, unrelated access, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: Outbound authenticated requests and access to PLAUSIBLE_API_KEY are sensitive but proportionate to querying Plausible analytics; users should understand that site identifiers and analytics queries are sent to Plausible.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill metadata declares the PLAUSIBLE_API_KEY environment variable and node binary requirement; no dependency installation, hooks, or automatic execution mechanism was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation description is broad for analytics requests, but the documentation and commands are scoped to Plausible-tracked sites and user-provided site IDs; no prompt overrides or hidden agent-control instructions were found.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The scripts perform read-only API requests and print JSON results; they do not write files, modify system state, install services, create scheduled tasks, or request elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose is Plausible Analytics reporting, and the shipped scripts only call Plausible stats endpoints for realtime visitors, aggregate stats, and breakdowns using a site ID and PLAUSIBLE_API_KEY.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want agents to use your PLAUSIBLE_API_KEY to query Plausible for site IDs you are authorized to access. Expect returned analytics such as visitors, pageviews, sources, pages, referrers, devices, browsers, operating systems, and countries to appear in agent output.
llm.findings:
[AE1] unexpected: SkillSpector reported partially inspected referenced scripts, but the local artifact includes stats.mjs, realtime.mjs, and breakdown.mjs and they were fully inspected; they contain straightforward Plausible API fetches, not analysis-evasion behavior.
[LP3] expected: The skill uses an API key and network-backed analytics queries, which is expected for Plausible integration. The metadata declares the required environment variable, though it does not provide enforceable endpoint-level tool scope.
[SQP-2] expected: The docs disclose PLAUSIBLE_API_KEY and Plausible API usage, and the scripts visibly send authenticated requests with site IDs. A clearer consent warning would improve usability, but the behavior is purpose-aligned and not hidden.
[SQP-1] expected: The description covers several analytics intents, but those intents match the stated Plausible analytics purpose and the included commands.
[A.I.G SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no T01-T09 security findings.
